name: @kitora/search
description: Kitora's search and data tools: a framework-free search core (ranking, grouping, facets, highlight, recents), a visual query builder model (AND/OR groups, typed operators, JSON, evaluation), a CSV import pipeline (parse, map, validate), and styled React parts for each.

exports.name: fold
exports.description:
Lower-cases and strips combining accents one source character at a time, so
the folded string has the SAME length as the input and indexes line up.
(Characters whose fold changes length, e.g. "ß" → "ss", keep their original form.)
exports.signature: (text: string) => string

exports.name: queryTerms
exports.description:
Splits a query into folded, non-empty terms ("  Big  Café " → ["big", "cafe"]). The kit's own
matcher (`createSearch`) still uses it internally.
exports.deprecated:
Use `queryTerms` from `@kitora/ui/highlight` (same name and result; it also folds
characters whose lower case changes length).
exports.signature: (query: string) => readonly string[]

exports.name: matchRanges
exports.description: Every range in `text` hit by any term, sorted and merged so overlapping hits become one range.
exports.deprecated:
Use `queryRanges(text, terms)` from `@kitora/ui/highlight`: same `{ start, end }`
ranges into the original text, and it accepts the raw query string as well as split terms.
exports.signature: (text: string, terms: readonly string[]) => readonly MatchRange[]

exports.name: highlight
exports.description: Cuts `text` into matched and unmatched segments for a query; no query gives one unmatched segment.
exports.deprecated:
Render ui `<Highlight text={text} query={query} />` from `@kitora/ui/highlight`, or
cut the segments yourself with `splitRanges(text, queryRanges(text, query))` from the same module.
exports.signature: (text: string, query: string | readonly string[]) => readonly TextSegment[]

exports.name: TextSegment
exports.description: One run of text: `match` is true for the parts a query term hit.

exports.name: MatchRange
exports.description: A half-open `[start, end)` character range in the original string.

exports.name: rank
exports.description:
Ranks `items` against `query`. Every term must match some field (AND), so
adding a word narrows the list. Ties keep input order. An empty query keeps
every item in input order with score 0.
exports.signature: <T>(items: readonly T[], query: string, fields: readonly SearchField<T>[], options?: RankOptions) => readonly SearchHit<T>[]

exports.name: localSearch
exports.description: The default source: `rank` over an in-memory list.
exports.signature: <T>(items: readonly T[], fields: readonly SearchField<T>[], options?: RankOptions) => (query: string) => readonly SearchHit<T>[]

exports.name: toHits
exports.description: Wraps items a server already ranked as hits (score by position, best first), for a custom `SearchSource`.
exports.signature: <T>(items: readonly T[], fields?: readonly string[]) => readonly SearchHit<T>[]

exports.name: applyFacets
exports.description: The items that pass every facet selection, optionally ignoring one facet (for its own counts).
exports.signature: <T>(items: readonly T[], facets: readonly FacetDef<T>[], selection: FacetSelection, ignore?: string) => readonly T[]

exports.name: facetCounts
exports.description:
Disjunctive facet counts: each facet is counted over the items that pass the
OTHER facets' selections. Selected values always appear, even at count 0.
exports.signature: <T>(items: readonly T[], facets: readonly FacetDef<T>[], selection: FacetSelection) => readonly FacetResult[]

exports.name: toggleFacet
exports.description: Toggles one value in a selection, dropping the facet key when it empties.
exports.signature: (selection: FacetSelection, facetId: string, value: string) => FacetSelection

exports.name: selectionSize
exports.description: Number of selected values across every facet (for a "Filters (3)" label).
exports.signature: (selection: FacetSelection) => number

exports.name: sortHits
exports.description: Sorts hits by an option; relevance (no `compare`) keeps the ranked order. Stable.
exports.signature: <T>(hits: readonly SearchHit<T>[], option: SortOption<T> | undefined) => readonly SearchHit<T>[]

exports.name: groupHits
exports.description:
Groups hits by `groupOf`, groups ordered by `order` (unknown groups after, by
their best hit) and each cut to `limit`. Hits keep their ranked order inside a group.
exports.signature: <T>(hits: readonly SearchHit<T>[], groupOf: (item: T) => string, options?: { readonly limit?: number; readonly order?: readonly string[]; }) => readonly HitGroup<T>[]

exports.name: paginate
exports.description: Slices one page. An out-of-range page clamps to the nearest real one, so a shrinking list never shows an empty page.
exports.signature: <T>(list: readonly T[], page: number, pageSize: number) => Page<T>

exports.name: pageWindow
exports.description:
Page numbers to show: first, last, and `siblings` either side of the
current page, with "gap" where pages are skipped. A gap never hides just
one page (it shows the page instead), so the strip stays the same width.
exports.signature: (page: number, pageCount: number, siblings?: number) => readonly PageToken[]

exports.name: runSearch
exports.description: rank → facets → sort → paginate in one call, the shape a results page renders.
exports.signature: <T>(items: readonly T[], request: SearchRequest, setup: SearchSetup<T>) => SearchResponse<T>

exports.name: SearchField
exports.description: A searchable field of an item. `weight` scales its score (a title outranks a body).

exports.name: SearchHit
exports.description: A ranked item. `score` is 0 for every item when the query is empty.

exports.name: MATCH_SCORE
exports.description: How well one term matched one value. Exact word > word prefix > anywhere.

exports.name: TermScorer
exports.description:
Scores one folded query term against one folded field value; 0 means no match. The ranking
adapter: pass your own (fuzzy, typo-tolerant, language-aware) through `RankOptions.score`.

exports.name: defaultTermScorer
exports.description: The default scorer: exact word > word prefix > anywhere, plus a bonus at the start of the value.
exports.signature: (value: string, term: string) => number

exports.name: RankOptions
exports.description: Options for ranking hits against a query.

exports.name: SearchSource
exports.description:
Where a search box gets its hits for a query: the data-source adapter. Return hits directly (an
in-memory list) or a promise (a server, a worker, a vendor index). `signal` aborts when the query
changes before the answer arrives, so a fetch can pass it straight through.

exports.name: FacetDef
exports.description: A facet: a dimension items can be filtered on. `get` may return several values (tags).

exports.name: FacetSelection
exports.description: Selected values per facet id. Within a facet values are OR; across facets AND.

exports.name: FacetValueCount
exports.description: One value of a facet: how many hits have it and whether it is selected.

exports.name: FacetResult
exports.description: A facet with its value counts, as a facet panel renders it.

exports.name: SortOption
exports.description: A sort choice. Without `compare` it means relevance (the ranked order).

exports.name: HitGroup
exports.description: One group of hits made by `groupHits`, cut to its limit.

exports.name: Page
exports.description: One page of items made by `paginate`, with the counts a pager shows.

exports.name: PageToken
exports.description: A page-number strip entry: a page, or a gap.

exports.name: SearchRequest
exports.description: What the user asked for: the query text, facet selection, sort id and page.

exports.name: SearchSetup
exports.description: What can be searched: the text fields, facets and sort options of a collection.

exports.name: SearchResponse
exports.description: The result of `runSearch`: the current page, the facet counts and every matching hit.

exports.name: pushRecent
exports.description:
Puts `query` first, dropping an earlier copy (case-insensitive) and
trimming to `limit`. Blank queries leave the list unchanged.
exports.signature: (list: readonly string[], query: string, limit?: number) => readonly string[]

exports.name: memoryRecentStore
exports.description: A store that lives only as long as the page.
exports.signature: (initial?: readonly string[]) => RecentStore

exports.name: RECENT_LIMIT
exports.description: Default number of recent searches kept.

exports.name: RecentStore
exports.description: Where recent searches persist. Both calls must not throw.

exports.name: nodeId
exports.description: A process-unique node id. Hosts that persist trees may pass their own ids instead.
exports.signature: (prefix?: string) => string

exports.name: emptyValue
exports.description: The empty value an operator starts with.
exports.signature: (operator: Operator) => RuleValue

exports.name: createRule
exports.description: A new rule on `field`, with the field type's first operator and its empty value.
exports.signature: (field: QueryField, id?: string) => QueryRule

exports.name: createGroup
exports.description: A new group, by default an empty, non-negated AND group.
exports.signature: (children?: readonly QueryNode[], combinator?: Combinator, id?: string) => QueryGroup

exports.name: carryValue
exports.description:
The value a rule keeps when its operator changes from `from` to `to`. Same
arity keeps it ("contains" → "eq" keeps the text); one ↔ many carries the
single value across; anything else starts empty ("eq" → "between").
exports.signature: (value: RuleValue, from: Operator, to: Operator) => RuleValue

exports.name: updateNode
exports.description: Applies `edit` to the node with `id`; returns the same root object when the id is absent.
exports.signature: (root: QueryGroup, id: string, edit: (node: QueryNode) => QueryNode) => QueryGroup

exports.name: addChild
exports.description: Appends `node` to the group `groupId`.
exports.signature: (root: QueryGroup, groupId: string, node: QueryNode) => QueryGroup

exports.name: removeNode
exports.description: Removes the node `id` anywhere below the root (the root itself stays).
exports.signature: (root: QueryGroup, id: string) => QueryGroup

exports.name: setRuleField
exports.description: Changes a rule's field, resetting operator and value when the type differs.
exports.signature: (rule: QueryRule, field: QueryField, previous: QueryField | undefined) => QueryRule

exports.name: setRuleOperator
exports.description: Changes a rule's operator, keeping the value when it still fits.
exports.signature: (rule: QueryRule, operator: Operator) => QueryRule

exports.name: countRules
exports.description: Counts rules in the tree (for "3 conditions").
exports.signature: (node: QueryNode) => number

exports.name: depthOf
exports.description: Depth of the deepest group, the root being 1 (for a max-depth limit).
exports.signature: (node: QueryNode) => number

exports.name: isRuleComplete
exports.description: Is the rule complete enough to apply? An incomplete rule (empty value) is skipped, not treated as false.
exports.signature: (rule: QueryRule) => boolean

exports.name: evaluateQuery
exports.description:
Does `record` pass the tree? Incomplete rules and empty groups are skipped
(an empty AND passes everything), so a half-built query never empties the list.
exports.signature: <R>(node: QueryNode, record: R, fields: readonly QueryField[], read: FieldReader<R>) => boolean

exports.name: countActive
exports.description: Rules in the tree that would actually apply (complete, known field).
exports.signature: (node: QueryNode, fields: readonly QueryField[]) => number

exports.name: describeQuery
exports.description: A one-line, human-readable form ("Status is any of Open, Blocked AND (Points > 3 OR …)").
exports.signature: (node: QueryNode, fields: readonly QueryField[]) => string

exports.name: toJson
exports.description: Serialises a tree to `QueryJson`, dropping ids (and values of operators that take none).
exports.signature: (node: QueryNode) => QueryJson

exports.name: parseQuery
exports.description:
Parses untrusted JSON (a string or an already-parsed value) into a tree,
checking fields and operators against `fields`. Collects every error
rather than stopping at the first, with a path to each.
exports.signature: (input: unknown, fields: readonly QueryField[]) => ParseResult

exports.name: FIELD_TYPES
exports.description: The value types a field can have; each has its own operator list.

exports.name: FieldType
exports.description: One of `FIELD_TYPES`.

exports.name: QueryFieldOption
exports.description: One choice of a `select` field: the stored value and its shown label.

exports.name: QueryField
exports.description: A field the builder offers. `select` fields list their `options`.

exports.name: OPERATORS
exports.description: Every operator. Which apply depends on the field type (`OPERATORS_BY_TYPE`).

exports.name: Operator
exports.description: One of `OPERATORS`.

exports.name: OperatorArity
exports.description: How many value inputs an operator takes: none, one, a range, or a list.

exports.name: OPERATOR_META
exports.description: Each operator's label in the builder and how many value inputs it takes.

exports.name: OPERATORS_BY_TYPE
exports.description: Operators per field type, the first being the default for a new rule.

exports.name: RuleValue
exports.description: A rule's value: nothing, a single string, a `[from, to]` range or a list. Kept as strings so inputs stay controlled.

exports.name: QueryRule
exports.description: A leaf of the query tree: one field compared by one operator against a value.

exports.name: COMBINATORS
exports.description: How a group joins its children: all must match (`and`) or any (`or`).

exports.name: Combinator
exports.description: One of `COMBINATORS`.

exports.name: QueryGroup
exports.description: A branch of the query tree: rules and nested groups joined by one combinator.

exports.name: QueryNode
exports.description: A node of the query tree: a rule or a group.

exports.name: FieldReader
exports.description: A record's raw value for a field; the builder never guesses property paths.

exports.name: QueryJson
exports.description: The serialised form: the tree minus ids, so saved queries diff cleanly.

exports.name: ParseResult
exports.description: What `parseQuery` returns: the parsed tree, or every problem found in the input.

exports.name: detectDelimiter
exports.description: Picks the delimiter that splits the first line into the most cells (outside quotes).
exports.signature: (text: string) => string

exports.name: parseCsv
exports.description:
Parses CSV text: quoted cells may hold delimiters, newlines and doubled
quotes (`""`); CRLF and LF both end rows; a BOM is dropped; blank lines are
skipped. The first row becomes `headers` (trimmed); short rows are padded so
every row has one cell per header.
exports.signature: (input: string, options?: { readonly delimiter?: string; readonly header?: boolean; }) => CsvTable

exports.name: autoMap
exports.description:
Maps each header to the best unclaimed field: exact name / id / alias match
first, then a header that contains a field name (or the reverse). Each field
is claimed at most once; unmatched columns map to null.
exports.signature: (headers: readonly string[], fields: readonly ImportField[]) => ColumnMapping

exports.name: mappingIssues
exports.description: Problems with a mapping itself: required fields with no column, and fields fed by two columns.
exports.signature: (mapping: ColumnMapping, fields: readonly ImportField[]) => readonly string[]

exports.name: mapRows
exports.description: Applies a mapping to raw rows. `firstLine` is the source line of `rows[0]` (2 when a header row came first).
exports.signature: (rows: readonly (readonly string[])[], mapping: ColumnMapping, firstLine?: number) => readonly ImportRow[]

exports.name: parseNumber
exports.description: Parses "1,234.50", "$12", "-3" etc.; NaN when it is not a number.
exports.signature: (raw: string) => number

exports.name: parseDate
exports.description: Parses an ISO date (`2026-03-04`) or a month-name date (`Mar 4, 2026`) into `YYYY-MM-DD`; numeric slash dates are rejected as ambiguous (03/04 is March or April). Null when invalid.
exports.signature: (raw: string) => string | null

exports.name: coerceCell
exports.description: Converts one cell to its field's type, or returns an error message. Empty cells are null (required is checked separately).
exports.signature: (raw: string, field: ImportField) => { readonly ok: true; readonly value: ImportValue; } | { readonly ok: false; readonly message: string; }

exports.name: validateRows
exports.description: Every bad cell across the rows: type errors, missing required values and duplicates of unique fields.
exports.signature: (rows: readonly ImportRow[], fields: readonly ImportField[]) => readonly CellIssue[]

exports.name: issueIndex
exports.description: Issues indexed by `row:field` for O(1) lookup while rendering a grid.
exports.signature: (issues: readonly CellIssue[]) => ReadonlyMap<string, string>

exports.name: coerceRows
exports.description: Typed records for the rows with no issues (the rest are reported as skipped).
exports.signature: (rows: readonly ImportRow[], fields: readonly ImportField[], issues: readonly CellIssue[]) => { readonly records: readonly Readonly<Record<string, ImportValue>>[]; readonly skipped: readonly number[]; }

exports.name: toCsv
exports.description: Writes rows back to CSV (the inverse of `parseCsv`), e.g. to download the rows that failed.
exports.signature: (headers: readonly string[], rows: readonly (readonly string[])[], delimiter?: string) => string

exports.name: CsvTable
exports.description: A parsed CSV file: the header row, the body rows padded to the same width, and the delimiter used.

exports.name: CSV_DELIMITERS
exports.description: The delimiters `detectDelimiter` considers, in tie-break order.

exports.name: IMPORT_FIELD_TYPES
exports.description: The value types an import field can have; each has its own validation and coercion.

exports.name: ImportFieldType
exports.description: One of `IMPORT_FIELD_TYPES`.

exports.name: ImportField
exports.description: A target field rows are imported into.

exports.name: ColumnMapping
exports.description: Field id per source column (index = column); null = column ignored.

exports.name: ImportRow
exports.description: One source row as field values, keeping the 1-based source line for messages.

exports.name: ImportValue
exports.description: A coerced cell value in an imported record; `null` for an empty cell.

exports.name: CellIssue
exports.description: A cell that failed, addressed by row index (into the mapped rows) and field id.

exports.name: localRecentStore
exports.description: A localStorage-backed store; falls back silently (empty list, no writes) when storage is blocked or absent (SSR).
exports.signature: (key: string) => RecentStore

exports.name: useControllableState
exports.description: `[value, setValue]` that follows `value` when it is defined, else internal state. `setValue` always calls `onChange`.
exports.signature: <V>(value: V | undefined, defaultValue: V | (() => V), onChange?: (next: V) => void) => readonly [V, (next: V) => void]

exports.name: useRecentSearches
exports.description: Recent searches with add / remove / clear. Pass `storageKey` to persist in localStorage, or your own `store`.
exports.signature: (options?: { readonly storageKey?: string; readonly store?: RecentStore; readonly limit?: number; readonly initial?: readonly string[]; }) => RecentSearches

exports.name: RecentSearches
exports.description: What `useRecentSearches` returns: the list, newest first, and its add / remove / clear actions.

exports.name: useSearch
exports.description:
Holds results-page state and runs `runSearch` over `items` whenever it changes. Keep `setup`
stable (module scope or useMemo). Uncontrolled by default (starting from `initial`); pass
`control.state` to keep the state yourself, e.g. in the URL.
exports.signature: <T>(items: readonly T[], setup: SearchSetup<T>, initial?: Partial<SearchState>, control?: SearchStateControl) => SearchController<T>

props.name: query
props.description: The search text.

props.name: selection
props.description: The selected values per facet.

props.name: sort
props.description: The id of the active sort option.

props.name: page
props.description: The 1-based page shown.

props.name: pageSize
props.description: How many hits a page shows.

exports.name: DEFAULT_SEARCH_STATE
exports.description: The state `useSearch` starts from: no query or filters, relevance sort, page 1 of 10.

exports.name: SearchController
exports.description: What `useSearch` returns: the state, the search response and the setters that change it.

exports.name: SearchStateControl
exports.description: Own the results-page state (a router's search params, a store): pass `state` and take every change from `onStateChange`.

exports.name: useSearchBox
exports.description: The search box's state machine; see the file header.
exports.signature: <T>(options: UseSearchBoxOptions<T>) => SearchBoxController<T>

exports.name: DEFAULT_LIMIT_PER_GROUP
exports.description: Default rows per group before the rest are cut.

exports.name: SearchBoxRow
exports.description: One row the arrow keys walk: a recent search, a hit, or the closing "See all results" row. `index` is its place in that walk.

exports.name: SearchBoxHitRow
exports.description: The row of one hit (`kind: "hit"`).

exports.name: SearchBoxRowGroup
exports.description: A group of hit rows, in display order. `total` counts the hits before `limitPerGroup` cut them.

exports.name: SearchBoxStatus
exports.description: Where the source is: nothing asked yet, waiting on a promise, answered, or failed.

exports.name: UseSearchBoxOptions
exports.description: Options of `useSearchBox`: the source, how hits group and what happens on select, submit and open.

exports.name: SearchBoxInputProps
exports.description: Props the parts spread onto their elements; exported so your own markup gets the same ARIA wiring.

props.name: ref
props.description: The input element, which the controller focuses (shortcut, clear, auto-focus).

props.name: role
props.description: The input is an ARIA combobox.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: The accessible name (the `label` option).

props.name: aria-expanded
props.description: Whether the list is showing.

props.name: aria-controls
props.description: The id of the listbox.

props.name: aria-autocomplete
props.description: The list suggests values for the input.

props.name: aria-activedescendant
props.description: The id of the active option; focus stays in the input.

props.name: aria-busy
props.description: Whether an async source is answering.

props.name: value
props.description: The current query.

props.name: spellCheck
props.description: Spell checking stays off for search terms.

props.name: autoComplete
props.description: Browser autofill stays off, so it does not cover the list.

props.name: onChange
props.type: (event: { readonly target: { readonly value: string } }) => void
props.description: Called when the text changes, with the event; sets the query.

props.name: onFocus
props.description: Called when the input gains focus; opens the popover.

props.name: onKeyDown
props.description: Called on each key press, with the event; moves the active row, chooses it or closes.

exports.name: SearchBoxOptionProps
exports.description: Props an option row spreads onto its element: its ARIA wiring and pointer handlers.

props.name: id
props.description: The option's id, referenced by the input's `aria-activedescendant`.

props.name: role
props.description: The row is an ARIA option.

props.name: aria-selected
props.description: Whether this row is the active one.

props.name: data-active
props.description: Present while this row is the active one, for styling.

props.name: data-kind
props.description: What the row is: a recent search, a hit or the "See all results" row.

props.name: onMouseDown
props.description: Called on mouse down, with the event; keeps focus in the input.

props.name: onMouseMove
props.description: Called when the pointer moves over the row; makes it the active one.

props.name: onClick
props.description: Called when the row is clicked; chooses it.

exports.name: SearchBoxState
exports.description:
The part of the controller that does not depend on the item type: what the `SearchBox.*`
parts read from context. `SearchBoxController<T>` adds the typed rows.

props.name: query
props.description: The query as typed.

props.name: trimmed
props.description: The query without surrounding spaces; empty means "show recents".

props.name: setQuery
props.description: Sets the query.

props.name: open
props.description: Whether the popover is open (always `true` for an inline box).

props.name: setOpen
props.description: Opens or closes the popover.

props.name: showList
props.description: Whether the list should render now.

props.name: status
props.description: Where the source is: idle, loading, ready or failed.

props.name: error
props.description: What the source threw or rejected with, while `status` is `"error"`.

props.name: active
props.description: The active row's index in arrow-key order, or -1 for none.

props.name: setActive
props.description: Makes the row at `index` the active one.

props.name: choose
props.description: Activates the row at `index`: a recent fills the query; a hit selects; "all" submits.

props.name: clear
props.description: Empties the query and refocuses the input.

props.name: variant
props.description: Whether the list pops over on focus or always shows inline.

props.name: label
props.description: The accessible name of the input and list.

props.name: shortcut
props.description: The focus key's binding, if any.

props.name: recent
props.description: The recent searches, if the box has them.

props.name: hitCount
props.description: Total hits for the trimmed query (before group limits).

props.name: ids
props.type: { readonly list: string; readonly recentLabel: string; readonly option: (index: number) => string }
props.description: The DOM ids of the list, the recent-group label and each option.

props.name: getRootProps
props.type: () => { readonly onBlur: (event: FocusEvent<HTMLElement>) => void; readonly "data-open": true | undefined; readonly "data-variant": string; readonly "data-status": SearchBoxStatus }
props.description: Props for the root element: its blur handler (closes the popover) and state attributes.

props.name: getInputProps
props.description: Props for the input element.

props.name: getListProps
props.type: () => { readonly id: string; readonly role: "listbox"; readonly "aria-label": string; readonly ref: RefObject<HTMLDivElement | null> }
props.description: Props for the listbox element.

props.name: getOptionProps
props.description: Props for the option row at `index` in arrow-key order.

exports.name: SearchBoxController
exports.description: What `useSearchBox` returns: the shared state plus the typed hits and rows.

exports.name: useImportWizard
exports.description: Drives an import of rows into `fields`. `finish` returns the typed records and the rows skipped for issues.
exports.signature: (fields: readonly ImportField[], adapters?: ImportAdapters) => ImportWizardState

exports.name: IMPORT_STEPS
exports.description: The import wizard's steps, in order.

exports.name: ImportStep
exports.description: One of `IMPORT_STEPS`.

exports.name: ImportResult
exports.description: The outcome of a finished import: the typed records plus the rows left out.

props.name: step
props.description: The step the wizard is on.

props.name: fileName
props.description: The uploaded file's name, or `null` before upload or when none was given.

props.name: table
props.description: The parsed upload, or `null` before upload.

props.name: mapping
props.description: The field id each source column maps to, by column index (`null` skips the column).

props.name: autoMapped
props.description: Field ids `autoMap` picked, so the mapper can badge them.

props.name: mappingProblems
props.description: Problems with the current mapping (`mappingIssues`): required fields with no column and fields fed by two columns.

props.name: rows
props.description: The mapped rows under review, with the user's edits.

props.name: issues
props.description: Every cell that fails validation, re-checked on each edit; empty before review.

props.name: issueAt
props.description: The issue message per cell, keyed `row:field` (see `issueIndex`).

props.name: result
props.description: The finished import, or `null` until `finish` runs.

props.name: load
props.description: Parses the uploaded text, auto-maps its columns and moves to the map step.

props.name: setColumn
props.description: Maps a column to a field (or `null` to skip it); a field taken by another column is freed there.

props.name: review
props.description: Applies the mapping to every row and moves to the review step.

props.name: editCell
props.type: (row: number, fieldId: string, value: string) => void
props.description: Changes one cell of a review row.

props.name: removeRow
props.description: Deletes a review row; it counts towards `ImportResult.removed`.

props.name: finish
props.description: Coerces the clean rows, moves to the done step and returns the result.

props.name: back
props.description: Goes back one step.

props.name: reset
props.description: Clears everything and returns to the upload step.

exports.name: ImportAdapters

exports.name: fold
exports.description:
Lower-cases and strips combining accents one source character at a time, so
the folded string has the SAME length as the input and indexes line up.
(Characters whose fold changes length, e.g. "ß" → "ss", keep their original form.)
exports.signature: (text: string) => string

exports.name: queryTerms
exports.description:
Splits a query into folded, non-empty terms ("  Big  Café " → ["big", "cafe"]). The kit's own
matcher (`createSearch`) still uses it internally.
exports.deprecated:
Use `queryTerms` from `@kitora/ui/highlight` (same name and result; it also folds
characters whose lower case changes length).
exports.signature: (query: string) => readonly string[]

exports.name: matchRanges
exports.description: Every range in `text` hit by any term, sorted and merged so overlapping hits become one range.
exports.deprecated:
Use `queryRanges(text, terms)` from `@kitora/ui/highlight`: same `{ start, end }`
ranges into the original text, and it accepts the raw query string as well as split terms.
exports.signature: (text: string, terms: readonly string[]) => readonly MatchRange[]

exports.name: highlight
exports.description: Cuts `text` into matched and unmatched segments for a query; no query gives one unmatched segment.
exports.deprecated:
Render ui `<Highlight text={text} query={query} />` from `@kitora/ui/highlight`, or
cut the segments yourself with `splitRanges(text, queryRanges(text, query))` from the same module.
exports.signature: (text: string, query: string | readonly string[]) => readonly TextSegment[]

exports.name: TextSegment
exports.description: One run of text: `match` is true for the parts a query term hit.

exports.name: MatchRange
exports.description: A half-open `[start, end)` character range in the original string.

exports.name: rank
exports.description:
Ranks `items` against `query`. Every term must match some field (AND), so
adding a word narrows the list. Ties keep input order. An empty query keeps
every item in input order with score 0.
exports.signature: <T>(items: readonly T[], query: string, fields: readonly SearchField<T>[], options?: RankOptions) => readonly SearchHit<T>[]

exports.name: localSearch
exports.description: The default source: `rank` over an in-memory list.
exports.signature: <T>(items: readonly T[], fields: readonly SearchField<T>[], options?: RankOptions) => (query: string) => readonly SearchHit<T>[]

exports.name: toHits
exports.description: Wraps items a server already ranked as hits (score by position, best first), for a custom `SearchSource`.
exports.signature: <T>(items: readonly T[], fields?: readonly string[]) => readonly SearchHit<T>[]

exports.name: applyFacets
exports.description: The items that pass every facet selection, optionally ignoring one facet (for its own counts).
exports.signature: <T>(items: readonly T[], facets: readonly FacetDef<T>[], selection: FacetSelection, ignore?: string) => readonly T[]

exports.name: facetCounts
exports.description:
Disjunctive facet counts: each facet is counted over the items that pass the
OTHER facets' selections. Selected values always appear, even at count 0.
exports.signature: <T>(items: readonly T[], facets: readonly FacetDef<T>[], selection: FacetSelection) => readonly FacetResult[]

exports.name: toggleFacet
exports.description: Toggles one value in a selection, dropping the facet key when it empties.
exports.signature: (selection: FacetSelection, facetId: string, value: string) => FacetSelection

exports.name: selectionSize
exports.description: Number of selected values across every facet (for a "Filters (3)" label).
exports.signature: (selection: FacetSelection) => number

exports.name: sortHits
exports.description: Sorts hits by an option; relevance (no `compare`) keeps the ranked order. Stable.
exports.signature: <T>(hits: readonly SearchHit<T>[], option: SortOption<T> | undefined) => readonly SearchHit<T>[]

exports.name: groupHits
exports.description:
Groups hits by `groupOf`, groups ordered by `order` (unknown groups after, by
their best hit) and each cut to `limit`. Hits keep their ranked order inside a group.
exports.signature: <T>(hits: readonly SearchHit<T>[], groupOf: (item: T) => string, options?: { readonly limit?: number; readonly order?: readonly string[]; }) => readonly HitGroup<T>[]

exports.name: paginate
exports.description: Slices one page. An out-of-range page clamps to the nearest real one, so a shrinking list never shows an empty page.
exports.signature: <T>(list: readonly T[], page: number, pageSize: number) => Page<T>

exports.name: pageWindow
exports.description:
Page numbers to show: first, last, and `siblings` either side of the
current page, with "gap" where pages are skipped. A gap never hides just
one page (it shows the page instead), so the strip stays the same width.

exports.description: rank → facets → sort → paginate in one call, the shape a results page renders.
exports.signature: <T>(items: readonly T[], request: SearchRequest, setup: SearchSetup<T>) => SearchResponse<T>

exports.name: emptyValue
exports.description: The empty value an operator starts with.

arity keeps it ("contains" → "eq" keeps the text); one ↔ many carries the
single value across; anything else starts empty ("eq" → "between").

exports.description: Applies `edit` to the node with `id`; returns the same root object when the id is absent.

exports.name: addChild
exports.description: Appends `node` to the group `groupId`.
exports.signature: (root: QueryGroup, groupId: string, node: QueryNode) => QueryGroup

exports.description: Removes the node `id` anywhere below the root (the root itself stays).
exports.signature: (root: QueryGroup, id: string) => QueryGroup

exports.name: setRuleField
exports.description: Changes a rule's field, resetting operator and value when the type differs.
exports.signature: (rule: QueryRule, field: QueryField, previous: QueryField | undefined) => QueryRule

exports.name: setRuleOperator
exports.description: Changes a rule's operator, keeping the value when it still fits.
exports.signature: (rule: QueryRule, operator: Operator) => QueryRule

exports.name: countRules
exports.description: Counts rules in the tree (for "3 conditions").
exports.signature: (node: QueryNode) => number

exports.description: Depth of the deepest group, the root being 1 (for a max-depth limit).
exports.signature: (node: QueryNode) => number

exports.name: isRuleComplete
exports.description: Is the rule complete enough to apply? An incomplete rule (empty value) is skipped, not treated as false.
exports.signature: (rule: QueryRule) => boolean

exports.name: evaluateQuery
exports.description:
Does `record` pass the tree? Incomplete rules and empty groups are skipped
(an empty AND passes everything), so a half-built query never empties the list.
exports.signature: <R>(node: QueryNode, record: R, fields: readonly QueryField[], read: FieldReader<R>) => boolean

exports.name: countActive
exports.description: Rules in the tree that would actually apply (complete, known field).
exports.signature: (node: QueryNode, fields: readonly QueryField[]) => number

exports.signature: (node: QueryNode, fields: readonly QueryField[]) => string

exports.description: Serialises a tree to `QueryJson`, dropping ids (and values of operators that take none).
exports.signature: (node: QueryNode) => QueryJson

exports.description:
Parses untrusted JSON (a string or an already-parsed value) into a tree,
checking fields and operators against `fields`. Collects every error
rather than stopping at the first, with a path to each.

exports.description: A leaf of the query tree: one field compared by one operator against a value.

quotes (`""`); CRLF and LF both end rows; a BOM is dropped; blank lines are
skipped. The first row becomes `headers` (trimmed); short rows are padded so
every row has one cell per header.
exports.signature: (input: string, options?: { readonly delimiter?: string; readonly header?: boolean; }) => CsvTable

exports.description:
Maps each header to the best unclaimed field: exact name / id / alias match
first, then a header that contains a field name (or the reverse). Each field
is claimed at most once; unmatched columns map to null.

exports.description: Problems with a mapping itself: required fields with no column, and fields fed by two columns.

exports.description: Applies a mapping to raw rows. `firstLine` is the source line of `rows[0]` (2 when a header row came first).
exports.signature: (rows: readonly (readonly string[])[], mapping: ColumnMapping, firstLine?: number) => readonly ImportRow[]

exports.name: parseNumber
exports.description: Parses "1,234.50", "$12", "-3" etc.; NaN when it is not a number.
exports.signature: (raw: string) => number

exports.name: parseDate
exports.description: Parses an ISO date (`2026-03-04`) or a month-name date (`Mar 4, 2026`) into `YYYY-MM-DD`; numeric slash dates are rejected as ambiguous (03/04 is March or April). Null when invalid.
exports.signature: (raw: string) => string | null

exports.description: Every bad cell across the rows: type errors, missing required values and duplicates of unique fields.
exports.signature: (rows: readonly ImportRow[], fields: readonly ImportField[]) => readonly CellIssue[]

exports.description: Issues indexed by `row:field` for O(1) lookup while rendering a grid.
